Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and immediate asks so we can model out costs/pricing for the three deployment paths (hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private VPC/on‑prem). High level notes from the call:

- Primary drivers: latency SLO ~150ms p95 for patient-facing inference, HIPAA compliance, data residency in US-east, and predictable monthly spend for budgeting.
- Current footprint you shared: ~8M tokens/day today, expected growth to ~12M tokens/day in 6 months; typical prompt length ~350 tokens; embeddings lookup volume ~50k vectors/day.
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline with daily peak windows (09:00–11:00 ET) where concurrent requests jump ~2–2.5x.
- Preference: Pilot via Dedicated (for predictable throughput) but legal/security needs may push to Private for long-term. Hosted API is acceptable for short PoC/early integration.

What we need from you to produce a short TCO and three scenario sketches (hosted, dedicated 1yr commit, private on‑prem):
1) Target procurement timeframe (Q4 / Q1?) and whether you require a vendor evaluation pack (SOC2, pen test) in advance.
2) Expected concurrency during peak (approx RPS or concurrent sessions).
3) Any bound constraints for rack/on‑prem costs (if private is considered) — rough % of infra you want to own vs Redwood manage.

Next steps I will take this week:
- Share an inputs workbook (attached) — fill the concurrency + procurement timeline fields and return.
- Build three high-level scenarios with assumed quantization, GPU types, reserve vs tokens math, and an ops/managed-services line item.
- Schedule a 30-minute follow-up to review the TCO and recommended pilot path.

Attachments: Polaris_TCO_Inputs.xlsx (please populate the yellow fields)

Thanks,

Tessa — good recap. A few notes on assumptions and what I recommend we include in Polaris' TCO deliverable: 

Assumptions to surface explicitly (we should show sensitivity on each):
- Model family and size: assume a 70B-ish decoder model (we'll include a cheaper/quantized option at 13B) — quantization impacts memory footprint and GPU choice.
- Token math: use your prompt length (350 tokens) + avg generated tokens per request (we'll show 6 / 16 / 32 buckets).
- Concurrency: produce scenarios for baseline, +1.5x, and +2.5x peak.
- Cost lines: per-token hosted API, reserved GPU amortized (1yr commit), and private host CAPEX + ops (annualized).

Deliverable structure (3 variants):
A) Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token + optional reserved throughput for predictable bursts; minimal integration lift.
B) Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pools): 1yr commit pricing, predictable monthly invoice, includes autoscale/burst policy; show break-even vs hosted at 6/12/18 months.
C) Private (VPC / on‑prem): itemize HW, rack, network, ops staffing, and integration cadence — called out as a longer procurement cycle and higher upfront.

Requests for the Polaris inputs workbook: exact target SLO (p95), expected retention window for KV cache (affects memory sizing), and whether embeddings need to be stored in-region only. The more granular the numbers, the tighter the TCO.

I attached the Redwood_Pricing_Playbook.pdf (internal) with typical unit-costs and GPU SKU baseline. I'll prep a quick sensitivity table and a suggested pilot config (Dedicated small pool for 4 weeks) so we can show two realistic pilot commercial options.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Tessa — thanks for the notes and Neha for the assumptions. Quick answers from our side so you can move forward with the modeling:

- Procurement window: aiming for vendor selection & commercial term signoff in mid-November (procurement review kicks off first week Oct, security review ~4–6 weeks).
- Expected concurrency: steady baseline ~25 RPS, peak windows up to ~60 RPS (roughly 2.4x baseline).
- Token volumes: current ~8M tokens/day, expected to hit ~12M tokens/day in ~6 months. Average prompt length ~350 tokens, generation avg ~12 tokens.
- Embeddings: ~50k vector lookups/day, must stay in-region (US-east).
- Compliance: HIPAA required; we'd need SOC2 + a data processing addendum.
- Preference: we want a Dedicated pilot if you can guarantee latency targets and an ops playbook; Private is on the table if procurement/legal push for it, but that would be later in 2027.

Attaching a short procurement timeline PDF and our internal checklist. We'll fill the Polaris_TCO_Inputs.xlsx this week and share by Friday. Let's plan the follow-up review for the week of Sep 6.
